newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil product stocks plunge on prompt sale.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil product stocks plunge on prompt sale.

text.p: Singapore residual fuel and middle distillate stocks fell to their lowest level in at least three years as refiners maximised their prompt sales to take advantage of the steep backwardation, traders said on Thursday.
"The figures show that the refineries here are dry," one trader said.
Stock figures released by the Trade Development Board (TDB) on Thursday revealed that residual stocks for the week ending April 2 fell by 2.435 million barrels to 8.229 million barrels.
Middle distillate stocks plunged 1.175 million barrels to 4.953 million barrels.
Light distillate stocks also dropped but by a marginal 322,000 barrels to 6.382 million barrels.

Industry sources said there was no incentive for both refiners and traders to store oil as the market was heavily backwardated which meant that prompt oil fetched a higher premium over those sold forward.

The physical to swap differential at its peak reached a hefty $2.50 per barrel for gas oil. In other words, a physical cargo for loading 15-days forward was traded at $2.50 per barrel above the swaps which is traded 30-days forward.
Traders said sellers looked to optimise their position by selling as much prompt cargoes as they could and locked such hefty premiums by hedging in the swaps market.
Sellers were able to achieve this because of the buying frenzy of local trader Hin Leong Trading who was willing to pay such big premiums for prompt cargoes in the local physical market.
Traders said Hin Leong will not be storing any of the oil it purchased on shore in Singapore as it has a large fleet of tankers, including five very large crude carriers.
The low stocks were also partly due to the shutdown of the 280,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Mobil refinery since March 16 for a six-week maintenance, traders said.
Also Singapore Refining Co only restarted a 90,000-bpd crude unit on March 23 after a schedueld 19-day turnaround and would only now build its inventories.
